content.json:
# CheckMate Health
API, frontend and infrastructure health from Application Insights, App Service and SQL logs, and Azure Monitor platform metrics.

## Health at a glance
API and browser telemetry from Application Insights. Server errors (5xx) mean something is broken and turn orange at 1% and red at 5%. Client errors (4xx) usually mean a caller sent a bad request, such as a duplicate name or a checklist that no longer exists, so they are shown but never colored. P95 response time turns orange at 1 s and red at 3 s. It's the P95 across every request in the time range, so it won't match the P95 under the response time chart's legend, which averages the P95 of each interval (as do the legends on the other percentile charts). **Overall** is the worst of the colored tiles, and health check uptime turns orange when there are no results, because the test runs every 15 minutes so that means it has stopped. API and browser errors count only exceptions that need attention: expected ones (API exceptions logged below Error, such as retried SQL connections; automated test traffic; and browser network errors the user recovered from, because a later API call in the same session succeeded) are counted separately and never colored. The exception tables on the API and Frontend tabs give the reason for each.

content.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend e = properties.essentials
| where tostring(e.alertRule) contains '__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/'
| where tostring(e.monitorCondition) == 'Fired' and tostring(e.alertState) != 'Closed'
| extend Fired = todatetime(e.startDateTime), Severity = tostring(e.severity), Condition = tostring(e.monitorCondition),
    Resolved = todatetime(e.monitorConditionResolvedDateTime), Resource = extract('[^/]+$', 0, tostring(e.targetResource)),
    Details = strcat('https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Monitoring_Alerts/AlertDetails.ReactView/alertId~/', replace_string(id, '/', '%2F'))
| project Severity, Alert = name, Fired, Resource, Details
| order by Severity asc, Fired desc
content.title: Active alerts
content.noDataMessage: No active alerts.

content.title: Health check availability (GET /health every 15 minutes)
content.noDataMessage: No health check results in this period.

content.query:
availabilityResults
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where success == 0
| project timestamp, location, message, ["duration (ms)"] = round(duration, 0)
| order by timestamp desc
| take 50
content.title: Failed health checks
content.noDataMessage: No failed health checks in this period.

content.query:
requests
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where url !endswith '/robots933456.txt'
| summarize Succeeded = countif(success == true), ["Client errors (4xx)"] = countif(toint(resultCode) between (400 .. 499)),
    ["Server errors (5xx)"] = countif(toint(resultCode) between (500 .. 599)) by bin(timestamp, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: API requests

content.query:
requests
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where url !endswith '/robots933456.txt'
| summarize P50 = percentile(duration, 50), P95 = percentile(duration, 95) by bin(timestamp, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: API response time (ms)

content.query:
exceptions
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| extend Source = iff(cloud_RoleName == "CheckMate.Web", "Browser", "API")
| join kind=leftouter (dependencies
    | where timestamp {TimeRange}
    | where cloud_RoleName == "CheckMate.Web" and success == true and isnotempty(session_Id)
    | summarize LastApiSuccess = max(timestamp) by session_Id) on session_Id
| extend Handled = Source == "API" and severityLevel < 3, Synthetic = client_Browser startswith "HeadlessChrome",
    NetworkError = Source == "Browser" and outerMessage has_any ("Failed to fetch", "Load failed", "NetworkError")
| extend Recovered = NetworkError and LastApiSuccess > timestamp
| extend Status = iff(Handled or Synthetic or Recovered, "Expected", "Needs attention"),
    Reason = case(Handled, "Logged below Error, such as a retried SQL connection",
        Source == "API", "Logged as an error",
        Synthetic, "Automated test traffic (CI smoke tests or Generate Load)",
        Recovered, "Network error; a later API call in the same session succeeded",
        NetworkError, "Network error with no later successful API call: the API was unreachable (cold start, outage or CORS) or the user gave up",
        "Frontend error")
| extend Series = iff(Status == "Expected", "Expected", strcat(Source, " errors"))
| summarize Exceptions = count() by Series, bin(timestamp, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: Exceptions: errors to investigate vs expected
Page views and users

content.query:
AppServicePlatformLogs
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| project TimeGenerated, Level, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 100
content.title: App Service platform events (restarts, deployments, container starts)

content.query:
requests
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where url !endswith '/robots933456.txt'
| summarize Requests = count(), ["5xx"] = countif(toint(resultCode) between (500 .. 599)),
    ["4xx"] = countif(toint(resultCode) between (400 .. 499)),
    ["P50 (ms)"] = round(percentile(duration, 50), 0), ["P95 (ms)"] = round(percentile(duration, 95), 0)
    by Operation = name
| extend ["5xx %"] = round(100.0 * ["5xx"] / Requests, 2), ["4xx %"] = round(100.0 * ["4xx"] / Requests, 2)
| project Operation, Requests, ["5xx"], ["5xx %"], ["4xx"], ["4xx %"], ["P50 (ms)"], ["P95 (ms)"]
| order by Requests desc
content.title: Operations

content.query:
requests
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where url !endswith '/robots933456.txt'
| extend Status = strcat(substring(resultCode, 0, 1), "xx")
| summarize Requests = count() by Status, bin(timestamp, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: Responses by status class

content.query:
requests
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where url !endswith '/robots933456.txt'
| where success == false
| summarize Failures = count(), ["Last seen"] = max(timestamp) by Operation = name, Status = resultCode
| order by Status desc, Failures desc
content.title: Failed requests by operation and status (5xx first)
content.noDataMessage: No failed requests in this time range.

content.json:
### Database calls
SQL dependency calls made by the API. Long spikes usually mean the serverless database was resuming from auto-pause.

content.query:
dependencies
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where cloud_RoleName != "CheckMate.Web" and type in~ ("SQL", "mssql", "microsoft.sql_server")
| summarize Calls = count(), Failed = countif(success == false) by bin(timestamp, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: SQL calls

content.query:
dependencies
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where cloud_RoleName != "CheckMate.Web" and type in~ ("SQL", "mssql", "microsoft.sql_server")
| summarize P50 = percentile(duration, 50), P95 = percentile(duration, 95), Max = max(duration) by bin(timestamp, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: SQL call duration (ms)

content.query:
dependencies
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where cloud_RoleName != "CheckMate.Web"
| summarize Calls = count(), Failed = countif(success == false), ["P95 (ms)"] = round(percentile(duration, 95), 0) by Type = type, Target = target
| extend ["Failure %"] = round(100.0 * Failed / Calls, 2)
| order by Calls desc
content.title: All outgoing dependencies

exceptions

| join kind=leftouter (dependencies
    | where timestamp {TimeRange}
    | where cloud_RoleName == "CheckMate.Web" and success == true and isnotempty(session_Id)
    | summarize LastApiSuccess = max(timestamp) by session_Id) on session_Id
| extend Handled = Source == "API" and severityLevel < 3, Synthetic = client_Browser startswith "HeadlessChrome",
    NetworkError = Source == "Browser" and outerMessage has_any ("Failed to fetch", "Load failed", "NetworkError")
| extend Recovered = NetworkError and LastApiSuccess > timestamp
| extend Status = iff(Handled or Synthetic or Recovered, "Expected", "Needs attention"),
    Reason = case(Handled, "Logged below Error, such as a retried SQL connection",
        Source == "API", "Logged as an error",
        Synthetic, "Automated test traffic (CI smoke tests or Generate Load)",
        Recovered, "Network error; a later API call in the same session succeeded",

content.json:
## Alerts
Alerts fired by the CheckMate alert rules in the selected time range. Azure keeps fired alerts for 30 days, so longer ranges only show the last 30 days. Every rule notifies the [CheckMate-Alerts action group](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__ACTION_GROUP_ID__/overview) (email and Azure mobile app push, plus Slack when the `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` secret is set); open it and choose **Test** to check notifications still arrive.

Acknowledge or close alerts, and see or edit the rules, in [Alerts](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/alertsV2). The rules are defined in `infra/modules/alerts.bicep`, and the [README](https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate#alerts) lists each one with its threshold. The **Investigate** tab says where to look when each alert fires.

The Service Health alert belongs to the subscription rather than the resource group, so it only shows here for viewers with at least Reader on the subscription. Budget notifications come from Cost Management rather than Azure Monitor, so they're listed separately under **Budget alerts**.

content.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend e = properties.essentials
| where tostring(e.alertRule) contains '__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/'
| where todatetime(e.startDateTime) {TimeRange}
| extend Fired = todatetime(e.startDateTime), Severity = tostring(e.severity), Condition = tostring(e.monitorCondition),
    Resolved = todatetime(e.monitorConditionResolvedDateTime), Resource = extract('[^/]+$', 0, tostring(e.targetResource)),
    Details = strcat('https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Monitoring_Alerts/AlertDetails.ReactView/alertId~/', replace_string(id, '/', '%2F'))
| extend MinutesToResolve = iff(isnull(Resolved), real(null), datetime_diff('minute', Resolved, Fired) * 1.0)
| summarize ["Times fired"] = count(), ["Still firing"] = countif(Condition == 'Fired'), ["Last fired"] = max(Fired),
    ["Average minutes to resolve"] = round(avg(MinutesToResolve), 0), Severity = min(Severity) by Alert = name
| extend ["Average minutes to resolve"] = iff(isnan(["Average minutes to resolve"]), real(null), ["Average minutes to resolve"])
| project Alert, Severity, ["Times fired"], ["Still firing"], ["Last fired"], ["Average minutes to resolve"]
| order by ["Times fired"] desc
content.title: Alerts by rule
content.noDataMessage: No alerts fired in this period.

content.json:
## Costs
What the CheckMate resource group costs, from Azure Cost Management. Every resource that makes up the app is in that group, including ones since deleted.

Amounts are actual costs in the billing currency, before any subscription credits. Cost data usually lags usage by 8 to 24 hours, so the most recent day is incomplete.

The **Spent this month**, **Budget forecast for this month** and **Monthly budget** tiles come from the `CheckMate-Monthly` budget (`monthlyBudget` in `infra/main.bicepparam`). The budget forecast is Cost Management's estimate for the whole calendar month, and the budget alerts when it passes 100%. The chart shows the actual cost of each day so far and Cost Management's daily forecast for the rest of the month; its legend totals both. The budget forecast is calculated separately from the daily forecast, so the two totals can differ. These tiles and the chart always cover the current month, whatever the cost period. Cost Management needs a few days of usage before it forecasts. [Cost analysis](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/costanalysis) has the full breakdown and budgets.

## Investigate
Where to look next when something on this page needs a closer look. Links open the Azure portal or GitHub.

**Live sites:** [Frontend](__FRONTEND_URL__) · [API reference (Scalar)](__API_URL__/scalar) · [OpenAPI document](__API_URL__/openapi/v1.json)

### Start here
| Question | Where to look |
|---|---|
| What is failing right now? | [Live Metrics](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/quickPulse) streams API requests, failures and exceptions as they happen. |
| Why did a request fail? | [Failures](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/failures): pick an operation or exception, then a sample to see its end-to-end transaction across the browser, API and database. |
| Where is a specific request or error? | [Transaction search](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/searchV1) by time, type, result code or text. |
| Why is it slow? | [Performance](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/performance) for API operations and dependencies, and [Query Performance Insight](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__SQL_DATABASE_ID__/queryPerformanceInsight) for the database. |
| How do the parts connect? | [Application map](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/applicationMap) shows the frontend, API and database with call rates and failures. |
| Is the API process healthy? | [Log stream](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_SERVICE_ID__/logStream) for live console output, and [Diagnose and solve problems](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_SERVICE_ID__/troubleshoot) for crashes, restarts and availability. |
| Has an alert fired? | The **Alerts** tab lists active alerts and the last 30 days of alert history; **When an alert fires** below says where to look for each one. Acknowledge or close them in [Alerts](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/alertsV2). |
| Is it Azure? | Resource health for the [App Service](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_SERVICE_ID__/resourceHealth), [SQL database](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__SQL_DATABASE_ID__/resourceHealth) and [Storage account](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__STORAGE_ACCOUNT_ID__/resourceHealth); [Service Health](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Health/AzureHealthBrowseBlade/~/serviceIssues) for Azure incidents affecting the subscription; and the public [Azure status](https://azure.status.microsoft/status) page. |
| Did something change? | [CI runs on main](https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain): every push to main deploys the infrastructure, API and frontend, then runs smoke tests. [Deployments](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/deployments) and the [Activity log](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/eventlogs) show every change made in Azure, including ones made by hand. |

### When an alert fires
| Alert | What it means | Where to look |
|---|---|---|
| API down | `GET /health` failed twice in a row. | **Overview**: Failed health checks shows the status code or error. A 404 right after a deployment usually means the infrastructure deployed but the API didn't. [Availability](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/availability) has every test result; **Infrastructure**: API startup log, and the [Log stream](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_SERVICE_ID__/logStream). |
| Resource health | Azure reports a CheckMate resource unavailable or degraded, for reasons on Azure's side. | Resource health for the [App Service](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_SERVICE_ID__/resourceHealth), [SQL database](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__SQL_DATABASE_ID__/resourceHealth) and [Storage account](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__STORAGE_ACCOUNT_ID__/resourceHealth). Usually nothing to do but wait. |
| Service health | An Azure incident or planned maintenance affects a service or region CheckMate uses. | [Service Health](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Health/AzureHealthBrowseBlade/~/serviceIssues) has the details and updates. |
| API server errors | More than 5 HTTP 5xx responses in 15 minutes. | **API**: Failed requests by operation and status, and API exceptions; [Failures](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/failures) for sample transactions. |
| API dependency failures | More than 10 failed SQL (or other) calls from the API in 15 minutes. A few failures while the database resumes from auto-pause are normal. | **API**: SQL calls and All outgoing dependencies; **Infrastructure**: Database errors and SQL connections. |
| Browser errors | More than 5 frontend exceptions in an hour. | **Frontend**: Browser exceptions, with the operation (load, save, delete) that failed. The alert counts every exception, so check the **Status** column: it fires during Generate Load runs, which only produce expected ones. |
| Browser API call failures | More than 5 API calls from the frontend failed in an hour. | **Frontend**: Browser calls to the API. If the **API** tab doesn't show the same failures, they never reached the API: check CORS and network errors. |
| CPU quota | The API used more than 45 of the F1 plan's 60 daily CPU minutes. | **Infrastructure**: CPU time. The app stops when the quota runs out and starts again when it resets. |
| SQL free offer running out | Less than 20% of the month's free vCore-seconds are left. | **Infrastructure**: Free amount remaining and App CPU billed. When they run out the database pauses until next month. |
| Frontend storage availability | Blob storage served less than 99% of requests successfully over an hour. | **Infrastructure**: Storage availability and transactions, and the [Storage account's resource health](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__STORAGE_ACCOUNT_ID__/resourceHealth). |
| Slow API | The API's average response time was over 5 seconds for 30 minutes. | **API**: Operations and SQL call duration; [Performance](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/performance). Cold starts and database resumes add a few slow requests. |
| Slow page loads | The 75th percentile page load was over 4 seconds in 6 hours. | **Frontend**: Page load time and Browser-observed API duration. |
| SQL storage | The database has used more than 80% of its maximum size. | **Infrastructure**: Data space used %. |
| Failure anomalies | Application Insights smart detection saw an unusual rise in failed requests or dependency calls. | The notification links to the detection; [Failures](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/failures) for details. |
| Monthly budget | The resource group passed 80% of its monthly budget, or is forecast to pass 100%. | **Alerts**: Budget alerts for the spend and threshold; **Costs**: Cost by service and Daily cost by service. |

### Logs and where they live
Everything below goes to the **CheckMate** Log Analytics workspace. Query it from [Application Insights Logs](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/logs), where the Application Insights tables have their classic names (`requests`, `dependencies`, `exceptions`, `traces`), or from [workspace Logs](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__WORKSPACE_ID__/logs) using the table names below.

| What | Table | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| API requests | `AppRequests` | |
| API calls to SQL and other dependencies | `AppDependencies` | |
| API exceptions and log messages | `AppExceptions`, `AppTraces` | |
| Browser page views, page load timings and checklist events | `AppPageViews`, `AppBrowserTimings`, `AppEvents` | |
| Browser calls to the API and browser exceptions | `AppDependencies`, `AppExceptions` | `AppRoleName == "CheckMate.Web"` |
| App Service HTTP logs | `AppServiceHTTPLogs` | Every request that reached the App Service, including ones the API never handled. |
| API console output | `AppServiceConsoleLogs` | stdout and stderr, including startup errors. |
| App Service application logs | `AppServiceAppLogs` | |
| Restarts, deployments and container starts | `AppServicePlatformLogs` | |
| Database errors, timeouts, blocks, deadlocks and automatic tuning | `AzureDiagnostics` | Filter on `Category`. |
| Changes made in Azure | Not in the workspace | [Activity log](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/eventlogs), kept for 90 days. |
| Deployments, database backups and migrations | Not in the workspace | Job logs of the [CI runs on main](https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain). The **Deploy Backend** job takes a BACPAC backup into the `db-backups` container of the [storage account](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__STORAGE_ACCOUNT_ID__/containersList) and then runs the DbUp migrations. |

### More information
- [README](https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate#readme): architecture, deployment and the Azure resources.
- [Generate Load workflow](https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate/actions/workflows/load-test.yml): sends realistic traffic to production to put data on this workbook.
- [Resource group](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__RESOURCE_GROUP_ID__/overview): every CheckMate resource in Azure.
- [Application Insights](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_INSIGHTS_ID__/overview) · [App Service](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__APP_SERVICE_ID__/overview) · [SQL database](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__SQL_DATABASE_ID__/overview) · [Storage account](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__STORAGE_ACCOUNT_ID__/overview) · [Log Analytics workspace](https://portal.azure.com/#resource__WORKSPACE_ID__/overview)
